# Closed package constructor arguments

Owned Java 8 declarations retain same-owner package constructor delegation
through a complete closed generic parameter on an ordinary extensible owner.
A generic factory executes before a provider getter and the selected
constructor. The closed container carries arbitrary raw contents.

Frozen direct, subclass and constructor method-handle callers check exact
visibility and metadata, virtual dispatch during receiver escape, partially
initialized final fields, argument snapshots, later element casts and exact
checked/Error identity at each evaluation stage. Source and SDK-provider
profiles must retain every original definition.

Recovered constructors require Java 25 because their argument evaluations are
retained before the delegating constructor call. Original inputs and the frozen
observer are compiled for Java 8; only owned recovered sources run on the JVM.

The `--nominal-sibling` source and SDK-provider variants add an original
`Class<?>` constructor beside the selected String constructor. String keeps its
complete SDK generic interface declarations. The fixed String argument view,
including null, excludes the unrelated class overload. All emitted Java units
compile, and the original metadata and exception attributes remain exact. The
sixty frozen behavior cases run twice in fresh JVMs; fifteen wrong programs
include deliberately selecting the nominal sibling. Native controls also cover
this/super delegation, checked exception declarations, range words, generic
interface metadata and incomplete or overlapping class declarations.

The variant also retains both original superclass constructors, so the String
view is checked on direct super delegation as well as same-owner delegation.

SDK argument headers and same-arity constructor siblings are resolved through
the canonical scope and erasure validator before this proof is consumed.

The `--ancestor-input` variants select a constructor whose fixed input inherits
a class with a marker interface. The complete original class chain excludes an
unrelated Class<?> overload. Seventy-two cases run twice in fresh JVMs; the
additional direct, reflective and method-handle callers observe the exact parent
constructor, aliases, partial receivers and null failure order. A future provider
subclass distinguishes field reads from virtual getter calls. Twenty-three wrong
programs qualify these observers, and all original definitions and metadata are
checked after compiling every emitted source.
